# Review Checklist: Kind Declarations

**Purpose**: Test whether the requirements for behavior preservation and for the single kind declaration are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable, across spec.md and the plan artifacts, before PR review
**Created**: 2026-09-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all five facts a declaration must state (name, version, arity, canonical file, parser) each tied to at least one requirement naming the reader that consumes it? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-004–FR-008]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec state which readers must read the declarations for the rejected-file slot bookkeeping, not only for the missing and duplicate checks? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK003 Is the set of kind-specific code where a kind name may still appear listed completely, including the cross-file rules that read individual kinds, not only the background-skills step, the many-file loops, and the rules data set construction? [Gap, Spec §User Story 2 Independent Test] _Resolved: User Story 2's list now includes cross-file rules._
- [x] CHK004 Is the line-count baseline for SC-004 anchored to a named commit in the spec itself, or only in the plan? [Completeness, Spec §SC-004, Plan §Constraints] _Resolved: SC-004 anchors 1103 lines at `0074436`._
- [x] CHK005 Does the spec state which existing docstrings and comments must change, beyond the load-bearing-order comment, or is the Assumptions clause the only coverage? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK006 Is it specified whether FR-011's "no hand-kept list" applies only to the final state or to every intermediate commit, given that the plan keeps derived views of the old tables for one commit? [Gap, Spec §FR-011, Plan §Commit 1] _Resolved: FR-011 applies to the final state; intermediate commits may keep only computed views._

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "hand-kept enumeration of kinds" defined precisely enough to tell an enumeration from kind-specific code, for example the explicit constructor or the cross-file locals? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002, §FR-011] _Resolved: FR-011 defines a hand-kept enumeration._
- [x] CHK008 Is "a count of kinds" in SC-005 defined clearly enough to say whether a test comparing a list of names to `["background-skills"]` asserts one? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-005, §FR-015, Research §R7] _Resolved: SC-005 defines a count; naming a kind is not one._
- [x] CHK009 Is "parsed exactly once" in FR-015 specified as a property of the declarations, of runtime behavior, or both, so a reviewer can tell whether a declaration-level test satisfies it? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-015] _Resolved: FR-015 states it as a declaration property, with why that suffices._
- [x] CHK010 Is "grouped by the module that owns each kind's parser" unambiguous for the three kinds whose declarations state no parser? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, Data Model §_KINDS]
- [x] CHK011 Is "one file or many" given a single representation across spec, data model, and contract, so the arity vocabulary is not left to interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Data Model §_Kind]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK012 Are the "six lists" of the input and the "five structures" of SC-002 reconciled in one place, with no requirement still counting six? [Consistency, Spec §Input, §SC-002, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK013 Is FR-010's explicit, field-by-field construction consistent with the plan's constructor reading a dict keyed by kind, and with FR-011's ban on presence checks naming each kind? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-011, Plan §Commit 3]
- [x] CHK014 Does FR-012's list of permitted edits to existing tests cover a shared helper added to the test module for the version-bump patches, or does that need stating? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Research §R6] _Resolved: FR-012 permits a shared helper for the bump tests._
- [x] CHK015 Are the per-kind values in the data model (version, arity, canonical file, parser) traceable to the tables they replace, with no value introduced by the plan alone? [Consistency, Data Model §_KINDS]
- [x] CHK016 Is FR-001's "parser if and only if the general loop parses it" stated identically in the spec, the data model's validation rules, and the contract's invariants? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, Data Model, Contract §Invariants]
- [x] CHK017 Is FR-014's "no CHANGELOG entry" consistent with the project rule that every user-visible change adds one, by an explicit argument that nothing here is user-visible? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §User Story 1]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK018 Can "nothing a user can see may change … for every input" be objectively verified, and does the spec or plan name the evidence standard beyond the existing suite? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, Quickstart §1c]
- [x] CHK019 Is SC-002's "five to one" measurable by a stated procedure rather than by a reviewer's judgment of what counts as an enumeration? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002] _Resolved: SC-002 cites FR-011's definition and a search procedure._
- [x] CHK020 Is SC-003's "one declaration plus genuinely kind-specific code" measurable, given it depends on the same undefined boundary as CHK007? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003] _Resolved via FR-011's definition (CHK007)._
- [x] CHK021 Is "the golden and contract corpora MUST NOT be edited" tied to a stated baseline so "unedited" is checkable? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, Quickstart §1a]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are requirements stated for a file declaring a known kind whose header is rejected at each distinct point (bad type, wrong version, kind differing from the packaged file at that basename), not only at "unsupported version"? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1 Scenario 3, Edge Cases] _Resolved: the slot edge case lists every header-rejection path._
- [x] CHK023 Is the unknown-kind problem's sorted-name requirement stated as a requirement, not only as an edge-case note? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-005] _Resolved: FR-005 requires the sorted listing._
- [x] CHK024 Is the asymmetric presence rule (surname tables required, careers not) stated in a functional requirement as well as in the edge cases, so it cannot be tidied away? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, Edge Cases] _Resolved: FR-008 forbids adding a career-presence requirement._
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for a packaged file that cannot be read, where only the canonical basename identifies its slot? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK026 Is the no-override path (the cached packaged load) covered by a preservation requirement as explicitly as override validation is? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1 Scenario 1]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK027 Is the assumption that the problem sort is a total order within one file stated with its source, and is the stop-and-reconsider response defined if it fails? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-013]
- [x] CHK028 Is the assumption that a version-bump test patch reaches every reader stated as a requirement on how the declarations are read, or left implicit in the plan? [Assumption, Spec §FR-012, Research §R2]
- [x] CHK029 Is the decision to exclude a `RulesData` field name from the declaration recorded with its rationale in a place a future reader of the spec will find? [Assumption, Spec §FR-010, Research §R1]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
